response.headline: Tunkhannock was a well-judged ultra: once the climbs are accounted for, you held 6:01–6:19/km across 50km and 1640m of climbing.

findings.title: Even effort once grade is accounted for
findings.body: Raw pace slowed from 6:06/km to 7:06/km, but grade-adjusted you went from 6:04/km to 6:14/km.

findings.title: The late climbs didn't break you
findings.body: Km 24–32 climbed at +2.8% and cost raw pace, yet your grade-adjusted split was 6:05/km.

findings.title: Carbs sat just under the ultra range
findings.body: You took 78g/hr, 2g/hr below the 80–120g/hr range for a 348-minute effort.

recommendations.action: Raise carbohydrate intake to at least 80g/hr for your next ultra.
recommendations.why: At 78g/hr you were 2g/hr under the low end of the 80–120g/hr range for a 348-minute effort.

recommendations.action: Use Tunkhannock's grade-adjusted pacing as the template for long, hilly races.
recommendations.why: Your split-to-split variation was 1.5%, against 4.7% at Hollow Road and 12.7% at Brandywine.

recommendations.action: Plan for heat if your next ultra is warm.
recommendations.why: Your one hot race, Brandywine Valley Marathon at 27°C, faded +32.7%, while you held even here at 6°C.
